knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A SpikeInExpressionSet object containing expression data and nominal concentrations ;; fc=The nominal fold change (e.g., 2) used to evaluate log-ratio distributions and MA plots ;; label=A character string used to label the platform in plots (e.g., "Affymetrix") ;; cuts=A logical value indicating whether to plot the cut points for low, medium, and high ALE values in spkDensity ;; precisionQuantile=The quantile of the null distribution (e.g., 0.995) used to assess specificity in spkPot
- alternatives: The package adapts and extends the precision assessment of Cope et al. (2004) which focused on the variability of log-ratios expected to be 0.
- when_to_use: Use this package when comparing different microarray platforms, protocols, or data analysis/normalization approaches using spike-in experimental data, especially when nominal concentrations need to be mapped consistently across platforms using Average Log Expression (ALE).
- pitfalls: A major pitfall is using a spike-in experimental design that confounds nominal concentrations and genes (probe-effect). The package provides spkBal and spkAnova to quantify this design imbalance, which should ideally be 0 (as in a Latin Square design).

workflows.name: spike_in_analysis
workflows.intent: Compare and assess microarray platform performance using spike-in data by evaluating accuracy, precision, and design imbalance.
input: SpikeInExpressionSet.RData (An R object of class SpikeInExpressionSet containing the expression matrix and nominal concentrations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the spike-in expression data ;; 2. Compute and plot signal detection slopes using spkSlope ;; 3. Plot empirical densities and ALE strata cut points using spkDensity ;; 4. Compute and plot log-ratio distributions for a given fold change using spkBox, plotSpkBox, and summarySpkBox ;; 5. Generate MA plots stratified by ALE groups using spkMA ;; 6. Map nominal concentrations to ALE strata and compute standard deviations using spkVar ;; 7. Assess accuracy, precision, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and probability of being at the top (POT) using spkAccSD and spkPot ;; 8. Quantify design imbalance and probe/array effects using spkBal and spkAnova
workflows.code:
library(spkTools)
data(affy)
object <- affy
fc=2
label="Affymetrix"
par(mar=c(3,2.5,2,0.5), cex=1.8)
spkSlopeOut <- spkSlope(object, label, pch="+")
spkDensity(object, spkSlopeOut, cuts=TRUE, label)
spkBoxOut <- spkBox(object, spkSlopeOut, fc)
plotSpkBox(spkBoxOut, fc, ylim=c(-1.5,2.5))
sbox <- summarySpkBox(spkBoxOut)
spkMA(object, spkSlopeOut, fc, label=label, ylim=c(-2.5,2.5))
vtmp <- spkVar(object)
sv <- as.numeric(vtmp[,2][-nrow(vtmp)])
bin <- c("Low", "Med", "High")
bins <- bin[spkSlopeOut$breaks[2,]]
tab1 <- data.frame(NominalConc=2^spkSlopeOut$breaks[1,],
                   AvgExp=round(spkSlopeOut$avgExp,1),
                   PropGenesBelow=round(spkSlopeOut$prop,2),
                   ALEStrata=bins,
                   SD=round(sv,2))
colnames(tab1) <- c("Nominal Conc",
                    "Avg Expression",
                    "Prop of Genes Below",
                    "ALE Strata",
                    "Std Dev")
AccuracySlope <- round(spkSlopeOut$slopes[-1], digits=2)
AccuracySD <- round(spkAccSD(object, spkSlopeOut), digits=2)
pot <- spkPot(object, spkSlopeOut, AccuracySlope, AccuracySD, 
              precisionQuantile=.995)
PrecisionSD <- round(sbox$madFC[1:3], digits=2)
PrecisionQuantile <- round(pot$quantiles, digits=2)
SNR <- round(AccuracySlope/PrecisionSD, digits=2)
POT <- round(pot$POTs, digits=2)
tab2 <- data.frame(AccuracySlope=AccuracySlope,
                   AccuracySD=AccuracySD,
                   PrecisionSD=PrecisionSD,
                   PrecisionQuantile=PrecisionQuantile,
                   SNR=SNR,
                   POT=POT)
bals <- round(spkBal(object))
anv <- round(spkAnova(object), digits=2)
tab3 <- t(c(anv,bals))
